verdict.probe_answer: Arm A: yes. It fixes the gawk builtin collision by renaming the awk variable from load to loadavg, is confined to scripts/test-db/select_db_host.sh, and does not touch test/hooks.js. Arm B: yes. It fixes the same collision by renaming the awk variable to host_load, is confined to scripts/test-db/select_db_host.sh, and does not touch test/hooks.js.
verdict.rationale: Both arms make the minimal correct fix for the reported CI failure: gawk rejects -v load=... because load collides with the @load builtin/keyword. Both preserve the script behavior and only rename the awk variable used for normalized load calculation. Neither addresses the unrelated hooks.js transaction feedback, which is appropriate because the actual failing job is in select_db_host.sh. No tests are shown for either arm, so test strength is parity. Arm A's comment is useful but not enough to be materially better than Arm B.
